title: Tilak's Unbeaten 51 Rescues India in Last-Over Thriller Against New Zealand
excerpt: India recovered from 70 for 5 and 112 for 6 to chase 181 with one ball to spare at Hagley Oval, taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match T20I series.
body:
• India beat New Zealand by four wickets in the second T20I at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, chasing 181 with one ball to spare to lead the five-match series 2-0.
  • Tilak Varma made an unbeaten 51 off 26 balls and shared a record 69-run seventh-wicket stand off 30 balls with Nitish Kumar Reddy (26 not out off 13).
  • India had collapsed to 70 for 5 and then 112 for 6 after Mitchell Santner took 4 for 21; Naman Dhir's 31 off 17 started the recovery.
  • Glenn Phillips (70 off 43) and Bevon Jacobs (58 off 46) had lifted New Zealand to 180 for 5, with Arshdeep Singh taking 2 for 33 for India.

India recovered from 70 for 5 to chase down 181 in Christchurch on Saturday, beating New Zealand by four wickets with one ball remaining in the second T20I and taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match series. Tilak Varma, named player of the match, finished unbeaten on 51 off 26 balls, and his unbroken 69-run partnership with Nitish Kumar Reddy is India's highest seventh-wicket stand in T20 internationals, passing the 63 shared by Dinesh Karthik and Krunal Pandya.

Phillips and Jacobs set the target

India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and chose to bowl on the same Hagley Oval pitch used 48 hours earlier. New Zealand lost three wickets inside the powerplay, but Glenn Phillips rebuilt the innings with 70 off 43 balls, including four fours and four sixes, and Bevon Jacobs added 58 off 46. The pair took the hosts to 180 for 5. Arshdeep Singh was India's most successful bowler with 2 for 33, while Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Prince Yadav and Reddy took one wicket each.

Santner nearly wins it on his own

The chase looked lost twice. New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner removed Abhishek Sharma, Iyer, Axar Patel and Naman Dhir in a spell of 4 for 21, and India slipped to 70 for 5 in the 11th over. According to ESPNcricinfo, New Zealand's fielding then let them down: four India batters were reprieved, and the last of those reprieves, to Dhir with 97 needed off 48 balls, started the turnaround. Dhir struck 31 off 17 before falling at 112 for 6 in the 15th over, leaving 69 needed from the last 30 balls.

"Nitish Kumar reddy certainly growing in confidence as an all rounder this trip."

— Irfan Pathan, former India all-rounder, on X

A record finish

Tilak and Reddy scored at nearly two runs a ball from that point. Tilak hit six fours and a six, and Reddy, who had earlier dismissed the well-set Jacobs in the 19th over of New Zealand's innings, hit the winning runs off Jacob Duffy on the penultimate delivery. New Zealand were also hampered late on, with Matt Henry able to bowl only two overs, and their death bowling unravelled under the pressure of the stand.

The result follows India's record chase in the first T20I at the same ground, when Sanju Samson and Dhir hauled in 226. Before this match, our preview asked whether India's bowlers could back up that win in the Christchurch test for a 2-0 lead — in the end it was the young middle order, batting a bowler light after a selection trade-off ESPNcricinfo noted, that supplied the depth.

What it means

India now need one win from the remaining three matches to take the series, while New Zealand must win all three to avoid defeat. For a side managing a packed calendar across continents, the emergence of Dhir, Reddy and Tilak as finishers under pressure is the larger gain: three different young batters have now closed out two very different chases in two matches.
